items.item: refusal without a permit NAMES the captain
items.evidence: Tool arm: a member's `permit` is refused, the refusal contains 'only this team's captain' AND the lead session, nothing written (readPermits []); a `wait` with no permit is refused with 'no permit' + 'your captain' + the lead session. Code: `captainSpelling()` names the recorded lead id, the no-team/no-captain facts, or the caller-is-captain fact.
Probe P6 (checkPermit at expiresAt → {reason:'expired'}); tool arm mints a 1 ms grant through the REAL tool, waits 5 ms and gets 'expired'.

items.item: a valid wait returns the answer or times out
items.evidence: Probe W2 (answer present → returned, 1 poll) and the tool arm: the answer arriving DURING the wait returns {ok:true, answers:[{questionId, answerTo, selected:['A. red']}], polls>1}; the timeout arm returns {ok:false, reason:'timeout', polls, waitedMs} after >=200 ms and well before the 5 s stuck-guard.

waitForReply is bounded TWICE: a wall-clock deadline and a poll ceiling ceil(timeout/interval)+1. Probe W1 timeoutMs 0 → 1 poll + timeout; W3 a FROZEN clock → 6 polls + timeout (ceiling, not hope); W4 an aborted call → 1 poll + 'aborted'. The tool caps the effective timeout by the request, WAIT_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS (60 s) and the permit remainder (probe P9), and every non-wait action stays immediate.

findings.title: PROCESS: T3 re-baselined the tool-surface constant (5,600 → 6,400) BEFORE reporting the measurement, against the captain's standing 'measure first, come back before changing' rule
findings.what: The number T3 recorded is correct and content-bearing (I re-measured 6,289 independently), but the constant was changed in the same step rather than reported and left to the captain. The captain conditionally accepted it; the rule breach happened regardless.
findings.why: A user-mandated guard whose bound can be raised by the very task it constrains is only a guard if the raise is authorised BEFORE it lands; measuring first is what keeps the guard honest.
findings.direction: The captain decides whether the conditional acceptance stands (the evidence supports it). For the remaining tasks: report the measurement and the proposed number, then change it only after the captain's word.

findings.title: The new comment says the permit/wait surface 'MEASURED 6,289 on top of the 5,414 above', which reads as a 6,289 delta rather than the new TOTAL
findings.what: The assertion measures the TOTAL, and the measured total is 6,289 (5,414 + 875). 'On top of' suggests 6,289 added to 5,414.
findings.why: A future reader cannot reconcile the comment with the asserted number (6,400) without re-measuring.
findings.direction: Reword to 'the whole surface now MEASURES 6,289 (5,414 + 875 for permit/wait)'.

findings.title: The wait answer carries `permitId`, but the tool's DECLARED output schema does not list it
findings.where: packages/mpd-team-core-plugin/src/index.ts · agent_teams_mail output schema vs the wait branch returns (`{ ok, reason, permitId, permitScope, polls, waitedMs }` / `{ ok:true, permitId, permitScope, answers|messages, polls, waitedMs }`)
findings.what: The schema declares ok/reason/permit/permitScope/answers/messages/polls/waitedMs but not permitId, while the tool returns it and the shipped arms assert `outcome.permitId`. Declared and actual output differ.
findings.why: A caller (and the schema-driven output checker) has no contract for a field the tool guarantees; a future schema tightening would break the arms.
findings.direction: Add `permitId: { type: "string" }` to the output schema (or drop the field and return it under `permit`), so declaration and behaviour match.
